claims.claim: Zepp Health's current app privacy policy applies to the Zepp app and bundled Amazfit devices and documents a broad set of captured, entered and derived health data.
claims.evidence: The policy names the Zepp app and Amazfit devices, then enumerates heart rate, SpO2, stress, PAI, PPG, HRV, ECG, body composition, exercise, sleep, cycle, mood, Readiness, Zepp Coach and food-diary data.

claims.claim: Zepp provides an authenticated privacy/export surface but does not publish a stable archive schema, metric inventory or historical-depth guarantee.
claims.evidence: The first-party portal exposes the Zepp app privacy workflow, while the public portal and policy provide no versioned archive file or field specification.

claims.claim: The current Zepp Android application describes storage access as supporting workout-data import and export.
claims.evidence: The official Google Play listing says storage is used to import or export workout data but does not enumerate formats or field coverage.

claims.claim: Zepp's public developer platform is an on-device mini-program platform for Zepp OS wearables rather than a documented personal cloud-history API.
claims.evidence: The official introduction describes a lightweight application framework for mini programs and watch faces on devices running Zepp OS.

claims.claim: Zepp OS exposes current, continuous, daily and resting heart-rate values on supported API levels, but the reference does not promise arbitrary cloud-history retrieval.
claims.evidence: The device API documents current/last readings, minute values for today, daily maximum, resting heart rate and callbacks.

claims.claim: Zepp OS exposes sleep duration, score, stages and naps through a permissioned device API.
claims.evidence: The reference lists score, total/deep time, start/end, stage intervals, current sleep status and naps, with API-level requirements.

claims.claim: The Zepp OS stress API exposes current, daily, hourly and seven-day windows rather than complete account history.
claims.evidence: The reference documents current stress, per-minute today data, hourly today data and past-seven-day averages.

claims.claim: Amazfit can automatically synchronize eligible activities to Strava after account linking; this does not establish general Zepp health-history transfer.
claims.evidence: Strava maintains a current Amazfit support page for automatic activity synchronization, not a complete health-account mirror.

claims.claim: Gadgetbridge supports local, cloudless synchronization with Amazfit devices but only for supported models and device-retained records.
claims.evidence: The project describes itself as a cloudless replacement companion with Amazfit support and points to model-specific support information.

claims.claim: huami-token retrieves Zepp/Amazfit device authentication material and tokens but is not a broad health-history exporter.
claims.evidence: The project documents separate Amazfit and Xiaomi modes and outputs device BLE keys, account tokens and assisted-GPS files.

claims.claim: The Mi Fit and Zepp workout exporter automates selected workouts through undocumented services but does not establish complete Zepp account coverage.
claims.evidence: The repository describes token-based export of workouts to several local formats and explicitly centers its scope on workout data.

claims.claim: Xiaomi Mi Fitness must be audited separately from the Zepp app even when legacy Huami names or Xiaomi-labelled devices appear in tooling.
claims.evidence: Mi Fitness uses Xiaomi's distinct com.xiaomi.wearable application package, while the Zepp app uses com.huami.watch.hmwatchmanager.
